KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: Placement is right and format is wrong. PLACEMENT, which is the harder half here, is correct and was verified independently: CR-307's AcroForm field names are shifted by one against its printed labels, so the widget named 'Defendants DOB mmddyyyy' is in fact the caption's defendant-name box and the widget named 'MOTION TO SEAL CONVICTION FOR' is in fact the DOB box. The build bound every CR-307 write to the printed label the widget was measured to sit against rather than to its name, and reading the delivered page 1 with pdftotext -bbox confirms it: 'Jordan Avery Reyes' lands at x=32.96 pdfY 672.86-682.11, the defendant-name line above the centred 'Defendant' caption at x=242.28, and '1991-04-17' lands at x=204.44 pdfY 643.03-652.28, on the 'Defendant's DOB' line whose label word sits at x=98.46 pdfY 641.38-657.43. CR-308's names are correct and its geometry independently agrees with CR-307's. All 20 values across both fixtures match their declared expected value exactly. FORMAT is the failure: CR-307 prints its DOB blank as 'Defendant's DOB (mm/dd/yyyy):' and CR-308 names the same widget 'Defendants DOB mmddyyyy', and the packet writes '1991-04-17' on both, in ISO-8601, on both the canonical and the boundary fixture. The packet demonstrably knows the rule — participant-instructions.md tells the participant to supply the conviction date 'in mm/dd/yyyy' for the blank it declines to write — and does not apply it to the value it does write. Nothing in production-field-map.json, reports/blanks.json, build-findings.json or either guide records a decision to deviate, so it is an undisclosed deviation from the official form's own printed instruction on a motion the participant signs.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: All 7 selfHelpStopConditions and both scopeRestrictions from the committed track record reach participant-instructions.md as exact substrings — tested here by literal substring match of each record string against the delivered guide bytes, 7/7 and 2/2, none merely paraphrased and none carried only in the filing guide. The track's first stop condition is that the whole track is a self-help boundary at the assessment stage requiring a named legal-aid or victim-services referral, and the guide states that in terms and tells a reader without that assessment that the packet is not ready to be used. Where the stop conditions are written to the operator rather than to the participant, this section says so explicitly — 'Some of those sentences are written to the people who build and operate this service rather than to you' — which is the right handling of mixed-audience record text and is why this obligation passes while REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING does not: the same disclosure is not made where the required-before-filing list needs it.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: filing-instructions.md sends the completed CR-307 with the proposed CR-308 to the clerk's office for the court that entered the conviction, in the underlying criminal proceeding, citing 15 M.R.S. § 2264(1), and adds that where several motions are filed the court consolidates them to one location. Both statements are the committed track record's own venue and destination fields, checked against data/record-clearing/legal-design-track-registry.json tracks[me-seal-survivor].venue and .destination. No court address, no division, no clerk's practice and no e-filing instruction is asserted anywhere that the record does not carry. The three court-for-filing boxes are correctly left to the participant because the route reaches Superior Court, District Court and the Unified Criminal Docket alike.

SERVICE.detail: Measured as a question about what the packet asserts, and it asserts only what the record carries. filing-instructions.md states that § 2264(3) directs notice to the prosecutorial office that represented the State, that the statute and CR-307 impose no service obligation on the movant, and that whether the movant serves the prosecutor or the court performs all notice, and by what method, is not settled in the committed record for this route. Checked against the delivered CR-307 bytes with pdftotext: the form carries no certificate-of-service block, which is what the guide says. The open source-acquisition gate me_2264_7_prosecutor_notice_method is declared in build-findings.json and named in the guide rather than papered over. No service method, deadline or proof-of-service requirement is fabricated. The residual is recorded under openLegalInputs and must close before this route could ever be delivered.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: The quantity FIX01 repaired is confirmed and is not what fails. All 11 requiredBeforeFiling strings from the packet-set manifest reach the delivered guides as exact substrings, tested here by literal substring match, 11/11, against 0 before the repair. What fails is that two of the strings published are addressed to the operator of the service and are now printed to the participant under the heading 'You must supply these before you file', introduced by the sentence 'These are the blanks on the forms themselves that this packet leaves for you'. (1) participant-instructions.md line 114 reads in full: 'No fee is expected, on the same analysis as the general sealing track: Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26) lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion. Confirm with the clerk and do not promise a refund.' 'Do not promise a refund' is an instruction to LegalEase about what it may tell a participant, printed to the participant as something they must supply. The same fee fact is rendered correctly participant-facing in filing-instructions.md, which drops that clause and says 'This packet states no fee amount. Ask the clerk.' — so the packet contains both the right rendering and the raw record string, in two guides, for the same fact. (2) Under 'Documents to gather', the guide introduces a block with 'On documentation of victim status in particular, the record says:' and then quotes 'Frame the question so a no carries no implication, and never ask the participant to produce proof.' That sentence is a questionnaire-design instruction to the builder, quoted to the participant as the record speaking to them, and it refers to them in the third person. The section's own framing does not cover either instance: it discloses only that 'Some of its entries record that nothing is required rather than asking you for something', which explains the bare 'none.' and 'none expected, because no fee is expected.' entries but says nothing about operator-directed text. The guide proves elsewhere that it knows how to make this disclosure, and makes it for the self-help stop conditions 80 lines earlier. This is DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE 'internal record text printed on a filing' — present, non-empty, in its section, verbatim from a controlling record, and therefore invisible to every counter — and it was introduced by the repair, because before it these strings were absent from participant copy altogether.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: Two option groups exist and both are correctly left unmarked. CR-307 and CR-308 each print 'X the court for filing' over Superior Court, District Court and Unified Criminal Docket; the track record's venue is the court that entered the conviction and this single route reaches all three, so no box may be pre-marked, and participant-instructions.md lists all six under 'Choices only you can make' with the record's own reason. CR-308's three GRANTED/GRANTED/DENIED ordering boxes are the court's election, not a route option, and are listed under 'The court fills these in'. Measured at 150 dpi: 0 added pixels in all nine square widget rects across both fixtures, so no option is marked and none is missing. reports/blanks.json also records one blank as notApplicableOnThisRoute, and the 30-field partition leaves no option unaccounted for.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: Measured rather than assumed absent. Every field name on both documents was enumerated from field-census.census-v1.json — 15 on CR-307 and 15 on CR-308 — and neither form carries a repeating row family: there is no indexed row set, no per-row cell group and no table. CR-307's item 1 is two free-text areas under one printed averment, and CR-308's paired 'A hearing was held on mmddyyyy' and '_2' fields are the two mutually exclusive ordering alternatives, not two rows of one table. The obligation does not arise on these forms and its answer is therefore that there are no rows to be incomplete. The charge-table risk catalogued in DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE — an AcroForm index disagreeing with a printed row number — cannot occur here because there is no numbered row set; the related name-versus-label risk does occur on CR-307 and is handled, and is measured under KNOWN_PREFILLS.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: filing-instructions.md states that the committed record expects no fee because Administrative Order JB-05-26 lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion, states no fee amount of its own, and tells the participant to ask the clerk. Checked against the track record: the same sentence is carried there verbatim, along with the record's own open question noting that the $60 post-judgment figure in that schedule is tied by its terms to civil rules and that the schedule separately provides 'Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee'. The record's waiver item reads 'none expected, because no fee is expected', and the packet accordingly asserts no waiver procedure, no form number and no eligibility test. No dollar amount, no waiver deadline and no clerk's practice is fabricated anywhere. That the raw waiver string is also dumped into participant copy is recorded under REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING; the fee treatment itself is correct.

visualDefects.detail: No visual defect remains on either fixture. Stray ink outside the declared write rects is 0 px on every page at 150 dpi, down from 469 px in nine synthesized check-box outlines before the repair; removed ink against the pinned sources is 0 px, so nothing the form prints was erased; boundary long values are set complete with no truncation and no collision with printed ink; page 3 is pixel-identical to CR-308 page 2. The two obligations that fail on this family are content defects in the participant guide and in a written value's format, and neither is visible to a geometry counter.

openLegalInputs.what: CR-308 page 2 prints a warning that a later conviction anywhere extinguishes the order. 15 M.R.S. § 2264(7) as amended by PL 2025, c. 513 provides that the subsection does not apply to records sealed under § 2262-A or § 2262-B, so the form's own printed warning contradicts the relief. Read on the delivered page 3 bytes here. The guide handles it by stating the statutory rule, quoting the form's printed words as the form's rather than as advice, saying the two do not agree and that the disagreement is unresolved, and naming the gate. That is the correct handling and it does not close the gate.

Whether the movant serves the prosecutorial office or the court performs all notice under § 2264(3), and by what method, is not settled in any committed record for this route. The packet states the settled part and refuses the unsettled part.

ROUTE_IDENTITY.detail: familyId 'co_municipal_conviction_seal-set' agrees across product-wiring.json, source-receipt.json, production-field-map.json, field-census.census-v1.json, build-findings.json, reports/rendered-artifacts.json, reports/actual-writes.json, reports/completeness-counters.json and reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json. The delivered pages print 'Petition to Seal Municipal Conviction Records' and 'Order to Seal Municipal Conviction Records' and cite C.R.S. § 24-72-708, which is the authority both guides name. The route is specifically municipal and the packet holds that distinction on the page: the caption city or town is refused by role on both forms with the recorded reason that the platform holds the county of the matter and a county is not a municipality, which is the correct refusal for a municipal court.

SOURCE_IDENTITY.detail: Both sources resolve exactly, recomputed here with sha256sum. official-form:JDF-683 = 6b451ae32c01ef1e637a460df627d246e1b4a61d4ac4f166005a7349fa87202e and official-form:JDF-686 = abf997d8e701df0c74b1eb7833b35f30c006b50bf71b019abf7754d898433200, both under MASTER_LIBRARY_SOURCE_DIR at STATES/CO/02_PACKET_FORMS. Page counts are 3 and 2, matching the 5-page delivered page manifest. Beyond the source bytes, this family pins five controlling records by whole-file digest AND by per-family entry digest, and this lane recomputed all ten with the builder's own stable serializer: every one of the five ENTRY pins matches exactly at this base. Two whole-file pins have moved — the track registry, edited by FIX03 for a Colorado sibling, and MASTER_QUEUE — and in both cases the entry pin proves the edit did not touch this family, which is exactly what the receipt's own 'whyBothPinsExist' note says the two pins are for. This is the strongest source and record binding this lane has read today.

COMPONENT_SET.detail: The packet-set manifest declares two components and only two: co_municipal_conviction_seal-primary-filing-1 (JDF-683, primary_filing, required, order 1) and co_municipal_conviction_seal-proposed-order-2 (JDF-686, proposed_order, required, order 2). product-wiring.json binding.packetComponents declares the same two identifiers, the MASTER_QUEUE entry declares the same two, and reports/rendered-artifacts.json carries both in componentSet and assigns every one of the five delivered pages to one of them. Both are delivered. Unlike this family's sibling there is no fourth or third form named anywhere and no gap to record. One observation, recorded and not scored as a missing component: product-wiring.json's generated proposedRepresentation gives component 2 the role 'companion_document' where the manifest says 'proposed_order', and points both components at the same canonical.pdf path and digest because the family ships one assembled packet. The binding block above it is correct; it is the generated specification that is loose.

KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: This is the obligation FIX04 repaired and it now holds on the bytes. The State line: the canonical fixture prints CO on the JDF 686 section-1 State rule and the boundary fixture leaves it empty, measured as 196 added pixels at that rect on canonical and 0 on boundary. production-field-map.json carries defendant-state under canonicalWrites and under boundaryRefusals with its unfittable record; reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json states in terms that 'the canonical fixture writes CO there, and the boundary fixture's spelled-out Colorado is refused as unfittable and left for the participant'; participant-instructions.md no longer lists the line under what the platform left blank and instead describes the check; filing-instructions.md makes no claim about it either way. Bytes, field map, near-miss record and both guides now say the same thing. The direction is the one the build's own rule supports: a value the platform holds is written onto the form's own measured printed rule wherever it fits, which is why the city and the ZIP either side of that same line are written too, and a value that does not fit is refused rather than shrunk below 6 pt or clipped. Placement was verified independently for all 16 writes by reading the delivered pages with pdftotext -layout and -bbox and matching each value to the printed label beside it — Defendant, Filed by Name, Case Number, Filed by Mailing Address, Filed by Phone, Filed by Email and item 2 Date of Birth on JDF-683; Case Number, Defendant, Defendant's Full Name, Date of Birth, Mailing Address, City, State, Zip Code and the section-3 Municipal Court case number on JDF-686 — and every drawnText equals its expected value on both fixtures. The dates are written in ISO-8601 (1988-04-17, 1961-12-31); neither Colorado form prints a date format anywhere, checked on both source binaries, so unlike this lane's Maine family there is no printed instruction being contradicted and this is recorded as an observation rather than a deviation.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.detail: Nothing the court, the prosecutor or the participant owns carries a mark this build made. Structurally, all four files — both delivered fixtures and both pinned sources — carry no /AcroForm, no /Widget and no /Btn, confirmed with pikepdf, so the synthesized-border failure mode has no widget to attach to and is impossible here rather than merely absent. Geometrically, a 150 dpi difference against the pinned sources over every protected rect gives 0 added pixels on both fixtures: the Division and Courtroom boxes on both forms, over which the form prints 'This box is for court use only'; the judge or magistrate signature and the order date on JDF-686 page 2; the petitioner's signature and date; and the item 14 certificate of service, which states that service has happened. Packet page 5, the page the judge signs, and packet pages 2 and 3 are pixel-identical to their source pages in both directions.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: Every value sits on its own printed rule and nothing sits anywhere else. Against the pinned sources at 150 dpi, added ink is 14652 px on canonical and 24340 px on boundary, and at a 2 pt tolerance 100 percent of it falls inside the declared write rects with 0 px outside on both fixtures; at 1 pt, 26 and 17 pixels respectively fall outside, and every one is within 2 pt of the bottom or side edge of an adjacent write rect, which is glyph descender and antialiasing on a 12 pt box. Removed ink is 0 px on every page of both fixtures, so no printed rule, caption or box was erased. Nothing is clipped: the boundary fixture's long values render complete — a 39-character hyphenated apostrophised name, a 45-character street address and a 25-character supplemental case number — and where a value genuinely could not fit at the 6 pt minimum the build refuses it rather than shrinking or truncating it, which is why the boundary email and the boundary State line carry exactly 0 pixels rather than an unreadable or cut-off value. On the narrowest rule on the sheet the write box is the form's own drawn rule read out of the page content stream, not a hand-entered coordinate.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: All 4 selfHelpStopConditions and the 1 scopeRestriction in the committed track record reach the delivered guides as exact substrings, tested here by literal substring match, 4/4 and 1/1. participant-instructions.md carries them under 'When this is not a do-it-yourself matter' and filing-instructions.md under 'Hand off to counsel when' and 'Scope restriction the record states'. The scope restriction that municipal courts are not on the state e-filing system and that the route must not be presented as statewide is carried in both guides and is also worked into the venue and filing sentences. The guide additionally opens by telling the reader that the record it is built from says C.R.S. § 24-72-708 was not read in full and that therefore nothing in the packet tells them they are eligible, which is the strongest self-help boundary on the family and is the record's own sentence.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: Both guides send the filing to the municipal court that heard the case and say that municipal courts are not part of the state e-filing system so local intake practice varies. Both sentences are the track record's own venue and destination strings, checked against tracks[co_municipal_conviction_seal].venue. No court name, address, division, e-filing portal or clerk's hours is asserted, and the guide records why: the platform holds no municipal court directory, so the Court Mailing Address rule on both forms is refused and carried to the participant rather than filled from something the record does not contain. The caption city or town is refused for the same reason on both forms, with the recorded finding that writing the county there would name the wrong venue on the face of both documents — which on a municipal route is the correct and non-obvious call.

SERVICE.detail: The packet asserts no service rule the record does not carry. Both guides state 'The source review does not state a service requirement', which is the track record's rules.service string verbatim, and participant-instructions.md adds the one thing the form itself establishes: JDF-683 carries a certificate of service at item 14 addressed to the prosecuting attorney, so the participant completes it after serving. Read on the delivered bytes: item 14 is on packet page 3, which carries 0 added pixels, so the certificate is left entirely blank — correct, because a filled certificate would assert that service happened on a filing nobody has served, and reports/blanks-left-for-the-participant.json records exactly that reason. No method, deadline, proof-of-service form or objection mechanic is fabricated; the guide states in terms that objection mechanics have not been confirmed.

REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING.detail: All 7 requiredBeforeFiling items in the packet-set manifest reach the delivered guides. Four survive a literal substring test; the other three are carried in substance and largely in the record's own words but split across a reformat, and this lane read each one to confirm rather than scoring the substring test — the CBI criminal-history report as a 'What the participant must obtain' entry in filing-instructions.md keeping the record's sentence 'Request a criminal-history report from CBI and attach it if the form requires it', the same item again in participant-instructions.md as 'Attach a current verified copy of your criminal history record, or file it within 10 days of filing the petition, as item 6 of the form says', and the signature and date item as a 'Manual completion items the record names' table row and again under what the platform deliberately left blank. Beyond the manifest list, all 28 unwritten measured rules and all 26 printed controls and underscore blanks are disclosed to the participant by page, section, printed label and what writing there says. The participant-facing sections are addressed to the participant throughout; the one place where operator vocabulary reaches the reader is the fee sentence, which is scored under FEE_AND_WAIVER because that is the obligation it belongs to and not because it is unimportant.

ARTIFACTS.detail: Recomputed here with sha256sum: canonical.pdf = 676d922f062ce75605d4aa1bd57cf16d6fe917ef408cfc82c49ae4863d3cb022 at 144207 bytes and boundary.pdf = 1c483f89703a4547c4a4ae1689ff3efa1b0be92c1aca12b17454138994a9e2b5 at 144266 bytes, both agreeing with reports/rendered-artifacts.json, with product-wiring.json, with the RASTER_QUEUE row and with the digest table printed at the foot of filing-instructions.md — five records naming the same two digests and all five right. Both files parse as 5 pages and every page differences cleanly against the source page its manifest claims. Both output-byte glyph readings exist and both reconcile against a recount of the non-whitespace characters actually drawn: canonical 107 + 96 and boundary 171 + 200, each equal to the recorded addedGlyphsReadFromOutputBytes for that document, with nonWhitespaceGlyphsOutsideMeasuredWriteBoxes 0 confirmed independently by the raster reading rather than accepted as a published zero. Recorded as an observation and not scored as a failure: those two readings are carried per source document in reports/actual-writes.json and are NOT carried per artifact in reports/rendered-artifacts.json, which also carries no rasterState field — so the file that product-wiring.json declares itself derived from is the one record here that omits them.

PAGE_ORDER.detail: Five pages in the order the manifest's component order requires: packet pages 1-3 are JDF-683 pages 1-3 (component order 1, the petition) and packet pages 4-5 are JDF-686 pages 1-2 (component order 2, the proposed order). Verified from the bytes and not from the manifest: each delivered page was differenced at 150 dpi against the source page its manifest claims and all five matched with 0 removed pixels, and the three pages the packet writes nothing on came back with 0 added pixels as well. The petition precedes the order it proposes, and within JDF-686 the signature page follows the ordering page.

ROUTE_OPTIONS.detail: Neither form draws a selection control this build could mark: all 22 printed controls across the two documents are the glyph U+2751 in the text stream rather than a stroked path or a widget, confirmed by the build's checkboxCandidates finding zero on all five pages and by this lane's own reading that the files carry no /Btn at all. The packet marks none of them, and participant-instructions.md says so under a heading that states it plainly — 'The tick boxes are yours, all of them, and you mark them by hand' — followed by per-document tables giving every control's page, section, the exact words printed beside it and what ticking it says, including the four mutually exclusive item 1 Petitioner options and the Municipal-or-District court election. The controlling record establishes no option the packet must pre-select, and on a route where the petitioner may be the defendant, a representative, a parent or an appointed representative, selecting one would assert a fact the platform does not hold. Nothing required is missing and nothing is asserted.

REPEATING_ROWS.detail: A repeating structure does exist here, so this was measured rather than dismissed. JDF-683 item 3, 'Agencies with custody of the records', repeats a name, case number and mailing address across Municipal Courts, the Colorado Bureau of Investigation, the Sheriff's Department, the District Attorney, the City Attorney, Law Enforcement and Other, and it runs from page 1 onto page 2. The packet writes into none of it: no declared write rect falls within item 3, and the 150 dpi difference gives 0 added pixels on packet pages 2 and 3. Every cell of every row is instead disclosed to the participant in the guide's must-supply table, row by row, with the CBI row noted as the one the form marks Required and prints the address for. Because no row is part-written, no row is incomplete, and the AcroForm-index-versus-printed-row failure catalogued in DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE cannot arise on a form with no AcroForm and no cell the build fills.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: The substance is right and the copy is not. Substance, all of it correct: the track record's rules.fees reads 'Unconfirmed. The fee must be confirmed before building.' and its waiver item reads 'The source review does not address a fee waiver', and the packet accordingly states no fee amount, no waiver procedure, no waiver form and no eligibility test anywhere, and participant-instructions.md gives the participant the action that follows from that silence — 'Ask the municipal court clerk what the fee is and what they need. Colorado's municipal courts are not on the state e-filing system and each one runs its own intake.' Nothing is fabricated. What fails is the delivered fee section of filing-instructions.md, which is filer-facing prose addressed as 'you' throughout, and reads in full: '## Fee — Unconfirmed. The fee must be confirmed before building. **Fee waiver:** The source review does not address a fee waiver.' 'The fee must be confirmed before building' is an instruction to the people who build this packet, published under the heading a filer reads specifically to learn what the filing costs, in vocabulary — 'building' — that means nothing to them. It is the DEFECTS_NO_COUNTER_CAN_SEE class 'internal record text printed on a filing': present, non-empty, under its own heading, verbatim from a controlling record, and therefore invisible to every counter. The page's opening frame does not cover it: it promises that where the record says nothing the page says nothing, and a build instruction is not the record saying nothing. Three mitigations are recorded because they bear on severity and not on whether the defect is there: the sentence asserts nothing false, the correctly addressed participant version exists at participant-instructions.md, and the same packet's open-items table discloses its build_blocker rows with a plain explanation of what they mean for the filer. The repair is one sentence — say that the committed record does not confirm a fee for this route and to ask the municipal court clerk — and this lane does not make it.

visualDefects.detail: No visual defect on either fixture. Removed ink against both pinned sources is 0 px on all five pages of both fixtures; added ink is entirely inside the declared write rects at a 2 pt tolerance, with the 26 and 17 pixels visible at 1 pt all lying within 2 pt of a write rect edge as descender and antialiasing spill; the three pages the packet does not write on are pixel-identical to their source pages; and both refused values leave exactly 0 pixels rather than a clipped or shrunken one. The border defect this cohort is being swept for is structurally impossible here: there is no /AcroForm, no /Widget and no /Btn in either delivered file or either source. The obligation that fails on this family is a sentence of prose and is not something a geometry counter can see.

theBoundaryRefusalThatReadsLikeARefusalO.theRecordedContradiction: reports/actual-writes.json and production-field-map.json record the JDF 686 State refusal as rect.width 27.25 against requiredWidthAtMin 24.3 at minFontSize 6. On its face 24.3 fits in 27.25 and the packet appears to have refused a value that fits.
theBoundaryRefusalThatReadsLikeARefusalO.verifiedNotAssumed: The refusal is SUBSTANTIVELY CORRECT and the RECORD is what is wrong. scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-text-fitting.mjs sets HORIZONTAL_PADDING = 4 and computes usableWidth = rect.width - HORIZONTAL_PADDING, so the comparison actually made was 24.3 against 27.25 - 4 = 23.25, and 24.3 exceeds 23.25. This lane reproduced the arithmetic independently rather than reading it off the source: embedding Helvetica with pdf-lib, 'Colorado' at 6 pt measures 24.28 pt, which is the 24.3 the record publishes, against 23.25 pt of usable width. The value genuinely does not fit and leaving it out is right — confirmed on the page, where the boundary State rect carries exactly 0 pixels.
theBoundaryRefusalThatReadsLikeARefusalO.soWhatIsTheDefect: The published refusal row omits the only number the decision was actually made against. A reader checking 24.3 against 27.25 concludes the packet refused a value that fits, which is what happened here before the arithmetic was run down. The shared module already documents this exact failure mode in its own header and exports usableWidthOf for it, and scripts/build-census-v1-nd-nonconviction-close-petition-set.mjs already annotates its refusal rows with usableWidth, exceedsUsableWidth and exceedsWidgetRectangle after the same confusion on a North Dakota family. This family's builder does not use it.
theBoundaryRefusalThatReadsLikeARefusalO.aThirdNumberIsAlsoInPlayAndIsCorrect: participant-instructions.md and the near-miss record say the rule is 31.25 pt wide. That is the printed rule the form draws, measured out of the page content stream at page 1, y=378.38, x 391.93 to 423.18; the write rect is that rule inset 2 pt each side, giving 27.25; the fitter then subtracts 4 and compares against 23.25. All three numbers are real and consistent, and only one of them — the 23.25 — appears nowhere in the delivered records.
theBoundaryRefusalThatReadsLikeARefusalO.notRepairedHere: This lane measures and does not repair. Nothing about this changes any delivered byte; it is a defect in what a record publishes about a decision that was correct.
